acceptanceCriteria: Every coded refusal carries an explicit retryability fact owned by Tasks, and the documented retryable set names each code and the condition under which a retry can succeed.
A test pins the classification for every code in internal/tasks/wire/codes.go, so a new code cannot ship unclassified.
Fencing codes (an attempt really lost) are never marked retryable.
body: Callers currently pattern-match result codes to decide whether to retry; the Flow-Proof runner killed healthy runs by treating LOCK_TIMEOUT as fencing, and now retries LOCK_TIMEOUT, SNAPSHOT_MOVED, STALE, REDO_PENDING, STORAGE_FAILED, HEAD_MOVED and JOURNAL_SATURATED by its own list. Requested by the owner in a beamfall/corvint issue 494 comment (2026-10-05T02:44:57Z, Flow-Proof fleet data point on main-cd70ba0: ~8,900 receipts, 13 concurrent sessions, pooled claim LOCK_TIMEOUT at rank 13; heartbeat/renew LOCK_TIMEOUT while the lease was FRESH was misread by the client as fencing). Needs a wire-contract change (taskman-command-result/0 or a successor profile) with a spec requirement, so the retryable set is owned by Tasks rather than each client.

completion.reason: Every acceptance criterion is met: absent-only retryable member (CAL-V0-078), wire.RetryOf classifying every section 11 code pinned by TestCALV0078_ClassificationCoversEveryCode, fencing never retryable. The retryable set is LOCK_TIMEOUT, SNAPSHOT_MOVED and REDO_PENDING, narrower than the reporter's client list. Evidence: docs/build-log/2026-10-04-v1-0780-retryable-codes.md at 618680492cf8. Verified at 618680492cf8 (merge of beamfall/corvint#574); CI on #574 green (go-product shards, go-interop, doc-gates). make gate, live store qualification and batch dogfood rebinding are NOT_RUN.

title: corvint-tasks: mark each command result's retryability explicitly (retryable: true) and document the retryable code set
